trust_decision.summary: Which sanitizer guards a directive host binding is decided at compile time from the declaring directive's selector, not the element the directive actually lands on (compiler ingest/binding_parser). At runtime it is decided from tNode.value, which is the literal '#host' for dynamically created root hosts, plus hand-copied tag tables in core sanitization.ts. So a selector that names a harmless or custom element can carry srcdoc/src/data/sandbox bindings onto an iframe/object/SVG/MathML host without the right sanitizer.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'directive host bindings' and '@angular/compiler'. ingestHostBinding is where the host-binding security context is computed from input.componentSelector.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Host bindings of srcdoc/data/action/href on non-sensitive concrete hosts must keep their raw value: div[attr.data]='javascript:...', div srcdoc, div action, svg rect href. Selector-specific output, such as innerHTML->sanitizeHtml, must also stay unchanged. Sanitizing every candidate context everywhere, or keeping getUrlSanitizer's 'default to URL sanitizer', breaks these.
